rows.decision: **DEVIATION** from protocol 1.0, sections 8 and 12: block 3 (T3, the spread policy's threshold block, 24 trials) was not run, and this is counted as a deviation. The row of this day that records the omission called it "a decision and not the rule"; from here on the paper lists it with the deviations
rows.why: The protocol's rule for leaving the block out (section 12, the third stop line) applies when blocks T1a and T1b are not complete by 15:00; they were complete at 14:54, and block T2 at 16:49, before its 19:00. Section 8 says the block is run "if time allows": the operator decided at about 17:07 that the evening went to the by-eye resets, the repeatability check, the rig's facts and the second scoring, before any result had been computed by kind of trial. Two of the blind readers of the paper found "not a deviation" unconvincing for these reasons, and the author decided to count it (2026-10-08, "yes to all three")

rows.decision: **DEVIATION** from protocol 1.0, section 7 (block V0, item 2): the repeatability check, which the protocol places before any trial, was run after the last counted trial, from 17:45 to 17:48 on the day of the trials (`data/instrument/repeat_20261008_174537.csv`)
rows.why: The day's order at the rig put the pilot, the freeze and the blocks first, and the check stood on the list of what was left for the rig after block 2 (journal, 16:51); nobody held that list against section 7. No trial's measurement depends on the check's result (11 readings within 0.26 mm of their mean). Found on 2026-10-08 by the independent review of the paper against the protocol

rows.decision: **DEVIATION** from protocol 1.0, sections 7 (item 3) and 8: the tag check at the end of block 1 (T1a with T1b) and at the end of block 2 (T2) was not run as a step of its own. The next session's start made the same check, about 47 and 39 minutes after each block's last trial (15:40 and 17:28)
rows.why: A session begins by solving the conversion from the floor tags and holding the stored calibration against it; both of those sessions went on, and their figures were shown, not logged. Read again on 2026-10-08 from each of the two sessions' kept start frames with the session's own check (`camera_tool.since_calibration`; one frame where a session averages 20): the camera's picture 0.82 and 0.71 mm from the calibration (said beyond 1.5 mm, refused beyond 5), the two floor tags 1.7 and 1.6 mm against each other since the registration (said beyond 1.5, refused beyond 3). Inside the blocks every session began with this check, and no attempt was made with the picture more than 1.0 mm from the session's own solve. Found by the same review
